t:
(a) 
Sections 802(8), 1072(1), 1073, 1208(a)(2)(B), 1213, 1444(a), 2733(f), 2771(b), 4537, 7204(a)(1)(D), 7205(a)(4), 7211 (a)(4), 7218(b). 7571(a)(3), 7572(a)(3), 7576(a)(3), and 9537 of title 10, United States Code, are each amended by striking out “Coast and Geodetic Survey” and inserting in place thereof “Environmental Science Services Administration”.
 
    (b) 
Section 1208(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding the following sentence flush at the end thereof: “For the purpose of clause (2) (B) of this subsection, active service as a member of the Environmental Science Services Administration includes active service as a member of the Coast and Geodetic Survey.”

fable.w: This section only makes conforming amendments, replacing one federal agency's name with another in title 10 and clarifying how active service is counted. A tempting reading is that references to agencies or service members might imply some coordination, but nothing here involves consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue by any party outside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the United States Code, specifically renaming a federal agency from the 'Coast and Geodetic Survey' to the 'Environmental Science Services Administration' and clarifying service definitions. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.

opus.w: This section only replaces "Coast and Geodetic Survey" with "Environmental Science Services Administration" in title 10, and says that service in the old agency counts as service in the new one. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. Changing an agency's name is boilerplate, not a process that brings outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to treat this as a change to an agency's structure or authority and therefore relevant to how decisions get made. That reading fails. The section only swaps one agency name for another in title 10 and adds a rule about how service time is credited. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in any decision.
